extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literary criticism; fiction writers interested in craft
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Henry James's principles from 'The Art of Fiction' to the writing or evaluation of literary fiction, emphasizing characterization, imagination, and realism while rejecting prescriptive moralizing and sentimentality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization versus plot (reject plot primacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: James disagrees with Besant’s assertion that plot is more important than characterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value deep, believable characters and allow characterization to drive the work rather than subordinating characters to an artificially dominant plot. Anti-pattern: privileging a contrived or sensational plot at the expense of character truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement of a 'conscious moral purpose'
rubrics_metrics.description: James disagrees with the claim that fiction must have a 'conscious moral purpose.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not force didactic moral lessons into fiction as a primary criterion of worth; allow artistic and aesthetic aims to stand on their own. Anti-pattern: evaluating or writing fiction primarily on whether it teaches an explicit moral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination as a legitimate creative tool
rubrics_metrics.description: James argues against the view that experience and observation outweigh imagination as creative tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit and cultivate imaginative invention alongside observation; originality and imaginative insight are valid sources of fictional truth. Anti-pattern: restricting fiction to mere reportage or literal transcription of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of mind (avoid superficiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: James responds that 'no good novel will ever proceed from a superficial mind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek intellectual and psychological depth in conception and treatment; good fiction reflects complexity of thought and perception. Anti-pattern: producing or approving work that is shallow, facile, or emotionally trite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject novels saturated with sentimentality or pessimism
rubrics_metrics.description: He decries the popular demand for novels that are saturated with sentimentality or pessimism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-reliance on cloying sentimentality or relentless pessimism as means to manipulate readers; aim for tonal balance and authentic feeling. Anti-patterns: melodrama driven by cheap sentiment; uniformly bleak works produced to satisfy vogue rather than truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to restrictive prescriptive rules
rubrics_metrics.description: James argues against restrictive rules for writing fiction advocated by critics like Besant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace artistic freedom and resist formulaic prescriptions about what fiction must be; evaluate works on their own artistic merits rather than checklist rules. Example guidance: prefer individual accomplishment and subtlety over compliance with rigid axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to literary realism (art of fiction as realism manifesto)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essay is described as a 'manifesto of literary realism' that challenges contemporary popular tastes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to render life with fidelity to its complexities and nuances while using imagination and characterization to achieve verisimilitude. Anti-pattern: superficial imitation of reality or pandering to fashions that distort truthful representation.
